rationale: Lens: contract stability. Judgment call A is ACCEPTED on the merits: R1.2's letter ('one derivation authoritative, the other removed or asserted-consistent') is satisfied because state.go's ctx.Phase/ctx.BeadID consumption is REMOVED outright — ResolveContextFromDir survives inside state show only transitively via ResolveTargetWithCache (target.go:125) as a specID resolver whose Phase is discarded — and Mode + ActiveBead now both derive from the same epicID resolution on one shared Cache (the same derivation atoms ResolveContext's WorktreeSpec branch uses internally). The implementer's regression argument is VERIFIED: ResolveContextFromDirWithCache's WorktreeMain branch (derive.go:627-636) takes no spec argument and leaves SpecID/Phase empty whenever >1 specs are active, so the literal ctx.Phase substitution would have broken `state show --spec <one-of-several>` from main. The bead-2 interplay is CLEAN: all v2/legacy machinery (readStoredPhase, LegacyPhaseSignature, hasV2Marker, the bead-2 replacement notice) is epic-scoped and a draft has no epic — the draft path sets ModeSpec directly without ever entering DerivePhaseWithStatus. R3.5 is genuinely served: the third deriving call site is gone from state show and discovery reads stored metadata without the mismatch warning, leaving exactly ONE warning-emitting derivation per invocation (down from up to 3). The suite failure observed in the bead worktree (5 cmd/mindspec next-ready-gate tests, .mindspec/phase.lock tripping the claim dirt guard) REPRODUCES AT THE PARENT COMMIT f12ce273 in a clean /tmp archive — pre-existing branch-level breakage from beads 1/2, not this bead. Two findings block: (1) the main-checkout draft probe is real-world vacuous — `spec create` writes the spec dir ONLY into the spec workspace, never the main worktree (internal/spec/create.go:89,117), so DiscoverDraftSpecs' os.Stat against the invoking checkout can never see a genuinely fresh draft from main; AC-1(iii) passes only because its fixture plants the dir on main, which the tool never does, so R1.4's 'draft-only state renders the honest draft representation' does not hold on a real main checkout — and the evidence IS visible from main (the spec/<id> ref is shared; the dir is probeable in the branch's tree). (2) This bead changed ResolveModeWithCache's error contract (derive error now returns "" instead of ModeIdle) and internal/instruct/run.go:134 swallows that error (`mode, _ :=`), letting Mode:"" reach instruct.Render which fails with the accidental 'loading template .md' error (instruct.go:207-213) — an unplanned NOW-reachable behavior change on a consumer no bead's declared file list owns. Neither finding fabricates state (both fail loud or fail idle-without-activeSpec), so no hard_block.
concrete_changes_required: Main-checkout draft discovery must see real drafts, or the limitation must be explicitly adjudicated: either extend the probe so a draft whose spec dir exists only on the spec/<id> branch/worktree is discoverable from the main checkout (e.g. a tree-scoped probe `git cat-file -e spec/<id>:.mindspec/specs/<id>/spec.md`, or scanning configured spec-worktree paths — the branch ref is already visible from main via shared refs), OR record the checkout-scoped limitation out loud: a deviation note on the bead (the commit says 'Deviations: none'), a sentence in the ADR-0023 amendment stating draft visibility is per-checkout and a fresh `spec create` draft is NOT visible from main, and AC-1(iii) reframed to name the fixture's premise (spec dir present on main) as the scenario it actually covers. As shipped, `spec create` (internal/spec/create.go:89 'never to the main worktree', :117 SpecDir(ws.Path,…)) guarantees the dir is absent from main, so DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache's os.Stat(root/.mindspec/specs/<id>) can never fire there and real main-checkout draft-only state still renders bare idle.

internal/instruct/run.go:134 must not let the changed ResolveModeWithCache contract produce Mode:"" → instruct.Render's accidental 'loading template .md' failure: handle the now-propagated error at the call site (return it, or render an explicit indeterminate/refusal naming the failed derivation) in this bead, OR have the tally record a written assignment of this exact line to bead 5 — bead 5's declared steps (instruct_tail.go, spec.go, internal/complete) do not currently include run.go, so without an explicit assignment the window has no owner.

Efficiency (small, this bead's code): reorder draftSpecStatusWithCache to consult FindEpicBySpecIDWithCache (memoized, free after the AllEpics health probe) BEFORE gitutil.BranchExistsIn — on an idle main checkout DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache currently spawns one git subprocess per historical spec directory (~30 in this repo) per `state show`, nearly all prunable by the free epic check since shipped specs have epics.

findings.title: Judgment call A: accepted — R1.2's letter is met by removal, and the literal plan reading verifiably regresses --spec
findings.detail: The 'one authoritative derivation' split (Mode+ActiveBead from ResolveModeWithCache + FindEpicBySpecIDWithCache + FindActiveBeadForEpicWithCache on one Cache; ctx.Phase/ctx.BeadID dropped from state.go) satisfies R1.2: within state.go's composition the other derivation is REMOVED, not merely paralleled. Verified the implementer's argument: derive.go's WorktreeMain branch resolves ambiguity purely from CWD, takes no spec parameter, and leaves Phase/SpecID empty for >1 active specs, so literal ctx.Phase substitution would break `state show --spec` on a multi-active main checkout. Residual: ResolveContextFromDir's own Phase fallbacks still exist for OTHER consumers — enumerated in R3-1. One honesty nit: the commit message claims 'Deviations: none' while plan §Bead 3 step 2's literal direction ('context derivation is authoritative') was inverted; the BRIEF surfaced it, but the deviation should have been self-declared.

findings.title: Disagreement-window enumeration: every remaining ctx.Phase consumer, with two items outside any bead's declared charter
findings.detail: Consumers of ResolveContextFromDir-family Phase at 7b6d83f1: (a) cmd/mindspec/instruct_tail.go:22 emitInstruct — every verb tail; draft-blind on main (WorktreeMain derives idle for 0 bd-active specs) and error-blind (ResolveContext's error is swallowed; nil/empty → fabricated idle Focus). Chartered to bead 5 — ACCEPTABLE AS NAMED, but with the carry-forward in R3-2. (b) internal/instruct/run.go:121-127 + handleNoState (run.go:211-213) — the standalone `mindspec instruct` verb (and the SessionStart hook): on a main checkout with a draft it renders idle 'Available Actions' while `state show` now says spec — a same-repo cross-verb disagreement reachable NOW; run.go appears in NO bead's declared file list, so this window currently has no owner (see also R3-3 for run.go:134). (c) internal/cleanup/cleanup.go:49 — Phase gates the 'spec still active' refusal; draft-blind from main (SpecID empty → guard no-op, a draft's worktree is removable without refusal) — PRE-EXISTING, unchanged by this bead, outside spec 128's requirements; note only. (d) internal/hook/hook.go:211 — ambient hs.Mode for hook state; draft-blind on main; never-block consumer, pre-existing. (e) internal/guard/guard.go:52 and internal/resolve/target.go:125 consume SpecID/BeadID only, not Phase — no window. Conclusion: no NEW contradiction was created among these consumers beyond the inherent one-surface-per-bead transition, but items (b) and R3-3 exceed bead 5's declared charter and must be explicitly assigned (bead 5 scope extension or a filed follow-up), not left implicit.

findings.title: Carry-forward to bead 5: its planned indeterminate-form trigger cannot see the in-worktree bd-failure class
findings.detail: Bead 5 step 1 keys the indeterminate form on 'context error or empty phase'. But ResolveContextFromDirWithCache NEVER returns a non-nil error, and in bead/spec worktrees it back-fills fabricated phases on bd failure (WorktreeBead error → ModeImplement, derive.go:601-605; WorktreeSpec error → ModeSpec, derive.go:617-619) — so from inside a worktree with bd down, emitInstruct will receive a well-formed fabricated Context and the planned trigger never fires, while `state show` (this bead) correctly refuses. Bead 5 must either rewire emitInstruct to the error-propagating ResolveModeWithCache family or stop derive.go swallowing errors; the tally should carry this note so bead 5's fix is not vacuous for the in-worktree failure class.

findings.title: Unplanned contract change lands on internal/instruct/run.go:134: swallowed error now yields Mode "" and an accidental 'loading template .md' failure
findings.detail: This bead changed ResolveModeWithCache to return ("", err) on derive/probe errors where it previously returned (ModeIdle, err). run.go:134 does `mode, _ := resolve.ResolveModeWithCache(...)` — the pre-image rendered fabricated idle guidance on a partial bd failure; the post-image sets mc.Mode="" and instruct.Render fails with 'loading template .md' (Render builds the template path as ctx.Mode+".md", instruct.go:207-213). Failing loudly is directionally what spec 128 wants, but this exact shape is accidental, names nothing, and carries no ADR-0035 recovery line — and run.go is in no bead's declared scope. Reachable when ResolveTarget succeeds but derivation subsequently fails (partial bd failure, git branch-check error in the draft probe). Fix at the call site in this bead or explicitly assign to bead 5 (concrete change 2). Positive side of the same coin, for the record: run.go:134's else-branch is now draft-aware for free — `mindspec instruct` from a draft spec worktree derives spec instead of idle.

findings.title: Main-checkout draft discovery is vacuous against real `spec create` output — AC-1(iii) passes only on a fixture shape the tool never produces
findings.detail: draftSpecStatusWithCache requires BOTH the spec dir (os.Stat under the invoking checkout's root) AND the spec/<id> branch. `spec create` writes the spec dir only into the spec workspace — 'never to the main worktree' (internal/spec/create.go:89, SpecDir(ws.Path,…) at :117) — and ADR-0023 main is merge-only, so a genuinely fresh draft's dir is absent from the main checkout until much later in life. From main: branch=yes, dir=no → not a draft → bare idle. AC-1(iii)'s fixture (newDraftFixtureRoot) commits the spec dir ON main, a state the shipped tool cannot produce. Consequences: R1.4's 'when discovery succeeds, the main-checkout output renders the honest draft representation for a draft-only state rather than bare idle' does not hold in the real flow; the same draft answers 'spec' from its worktree and 'idle' from main. Mitigations acknowledged: bare idle carries no activeSpec (R1.1's unconditional core holds), and the ADR-0023 amendment's 'filesystem-scoped' wording makes the behavior internally consistent per checkout. But the evidence needed IS visible from main — the branch ref is shared, and the dir is probeable tree-scoped (`git cat-file -e spec/<id>:.mindspec/specs/<id>/spec.md`) or via the spec worktree path. Fix the probe's reach or adjudicate + document the limitation explicitly (concrete change 1); silence is the one disallowed disposition in this spec.

findings.title: Idle-main `state show` now costs one git subprocess per historical spec directory
findings.detail: DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache enumerates every dir under .mindspec/specs (~30 on this repo's main) and draftSpecStatusWithCache calls gitutil.BranchExistsIn (a git subprocess) BEFORE the free memoized FindEpicBySpecIDWithCache check. Shipped specs (dir on main, epic exists) would be pruned by the epic check without any subprocess; as ordered, each costs a git call. Only hit on the healthy-bd zero-active path, but that is the common idle case. Reorder the checks (concrete change 3).

findings.title: Bead-2 interplay clean; R3.5 one-Cache recomposition genuinely reduces the warning class; behavior deltas worth the bead-4 table's awareness
findings.detail: (i) Drafts cannot misfire any v2/legacy path: readStoredPhase / LegacyPhaseSignature / hasV2Marker / the bead-2 replacement notice are all epic-scoped and the draft path returns ModeSpec before DerivePhaseWithStatus is reachable; state show performs no writes and never calls EnsureMigrated. (ii) R3.5: state show now holds one Cache; the ResolveContextFromDir deriving call site is gone and DiscoverActiveSpecs reads stored metadata (extractPhaseFromMetadata) without the mismatch warning, so exactly ONE stored-vs-derived warning site (ResolveModeWithCache → DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache) remains per invocation — a real reduction of the up-to-3x class. Note the Cache memoizes bd queries, not derivations, so the dedupe holds because one deriving call remains, not because emission is memoized. (iii) Visible output delta for bead 4's agreement table: in a bead worktree, activeBead is now the epic's bd-claimed in_progress bead (FindActiveBeadForEpicWithCache) rather than the CWD-path bead — bd-authoritative per ADR-0023 and an improvement, but a change in what the field means. (iv) The two composition-allowlist entries are house-pattern conformant (waist + early-gate rationale matching neighbors; DiscoverDraftSpecsWithCache idvalidate.SpecID-gates enumerated names before composing paths, matching spec.List's convention).

findings.title: NOT this bead: spec-branch suite is red — 5 cmd/mindspec next-ready-gate tests fail via a stray .mindspec/phase.lock, reproducing at the parent commit
findings.detail: go test ./cmd/mindspec at 7b6d83f1 fails 5 tests (TestBeadReadyCheck_TemporalFlow_RealPlanApproveAndComplete, TestNextReadyGate_{NegativeBead_RefusalIsZeroMutationAndForceOrthogonal, AllowNotReady_ClaimsAndRecordsDurableMarker, PositiveBead_ClaimsWithNoPromptNoRefusal, AllowNotReady_ClaimFailureRollsBackMarker}): the R3.3 phase lock file (.mindspec/phase.lock, internal/phase/phaselock.go:48) is created inside the spec-124 fixture repos, whose .gitignore lacks the entry the real repo has (.gitignore:10), and `next`'s dirty-tree guard then refuses with 'uncommitted user changes: .mindspec/phase.lock'. ATTRIBUTION VERIFIED: the same test fails identically at parent f12ce273 in a clean /tmp git-archive checkout — this is bead-1/2 fallout (the lock writer needs to ensure-ignore via gitutil/gitignore.go, or the guard needs the lock file in its never-blocks set), pre-existing on the branch and NOT caused by this bead. It does not count against bead 3's gate, but the branch is not suite-green and this must be fixed (and owned — likely a bead-1/2 fix-up) before bead 4 or the final review; internal/resolve, internal/phase, internal/lint all pass at 7b6d83f1.
